transcript.content: Hello, welcome to the clinic. Can you tell me what brings you in today?

Hi. Um, well, I came in because... I've been having this issue with food lately. Like, after everyone goes to bed, I’ll tell myself I’m just going down to the kitchen to have a little bit of leftovers. My husband is usually asleep by 10, he's a really heavy sleeper. But then... I don't know, suddenly I realize I’ve eaten half a tray of catered pasta. 

We do a lot of catering at my job—I'm a marketing manager, and we just had this huge product launch last week. The venue was absolutely gorgeous, but trying to coordinate the A/V team with the catering staff was a complete nightmare. They literally set up the buffet right next to the main speakers! It was so loud. Anyway, I brought the extra food home. 

So I'll eat all that pasta, and then I'll eat the leftover dessert from a client dinner, and then just... whatever snacks are in the pantry, all in one sitting. Which is honestly so frustrating because I just reorganized that pantry. I bought all those clear plastic bins from the Container Store to make it look nice, you know? But my kids just throw the empty granola bar boxes back in there instead of the recycling. It's like talking to a wall trying to get them to keep it tidy. But, um... yeah, the eating all that at night. That's why I made the appointment.
Do you feel like you can't stop eating or control what or how much you're eating during these nighttime episodes?

Yeah, that's exactly it. It's like... once I start, especially after a tense night with my husband. We've been bickering so much lately about the house, actually. We're trying to get the guest bathroom remodeled before my in-laws visit for Thanksgiving, and the contractor he hired is just... well, he never shows up on time. I told Greg we should have gone with the company my coworker recommended, but he wanted to save a few hundred dollars. And now the subway tile I picked out is backordered until November anyway! It's just so stressful, because his mother notices absolutely everything. If there's a speck of dust on the baseboards, she makes a little passive-aggressive comment. I really don't have the patience for it this year. 

But, um, anyway... right, the eating. Yeah, so after an evening like that, it feels like the decision-making part of me just completely goes offline. I just keep reaching for more and more food, even while I'm actively thinking to myself, 'Patricia, stop, this is enough.' But I just... I can't seem to make myself stop.
After these nighttime eating episodes, do you ever try to compensate for the amount you've eaten by making yourself vomit, using laxatives, or exercising a lot more than usual?

Oh, no, no, I don't do anything like that. I definitely don't make myself sick or take laxatives or anything. And exercise? Ha. I wish I had the time. I actually bought a Peloton last year during the Black Friday sales. It was such a good deal, they threw in the shoes and the little hand weights for free. But honestly, it's just turned into a very expensive clothing rack in the corner of our bedroom. 

Greg constantly drapes his work shirts over the handlebars, which drives me absolutely crazy because I bought him a really nice valet stand for our anniversary. It's solid mahogany, matches our dresser perfectly, but does he use it? No. He just tosses things wherever he feels like it. It's like living with a teenager sometimes. My actual teenager, Chloe, is somehow neater than he is right now, though she's been hoarding half-empty water cups on her nightstand again, which leaves those awful little water rings on the wood... 

Wait, what were we talking about? Oh, right, making up for the eating. No, I don't do any of that stuff. I just wake up and feel terrible about it.
Do you find yourself eating much more quickly than usual during these nighttime eating episodes, or do you often keep eating until you feel uncomfortably full?

Yeah, I do. I mean, I eat so fast standing at the kitchen island or while I'm scrolling through work emails that I barely even taste it. It's like I'm on autopilot. Sometimes I'll look down and the containers are just empty before I've really even registered what I was eating. Which reminds me, I need to email the caterer from that launch event because they still haven't sent the finalized invoice, and accounting is breathing down my neck about the quarterly budget close. Our CFO is a real stickler for deadlines. Last quarter, he sent out this company-wide memo in all caps about expense reports, which I thought was incredibly unprofessional. I mean, we're adults, not middle schoolers. 

And speaking of middle schoolers, my son's soccer schedule has been absolutely chaotic lately. They changed the practice fields at the last minute because of the rain, so now I have to drive all the way across town during rush hour. The traffic on I-95 is just unbearable at 5:30. I tried to find a carpool, but the other moms in the neighborhood are all so cliquey. There's this one mom, Susan, who always volunteers to bring the snacks, but then she brings these organic, sugar-free, gluten-free cardboard things that the kids won't even touch. I mean, just bring orange slices and Capri Sun like a normal person, you know? 

But, um... wait, yes. I definitely eat way faster than normal. And I don't really stop until I feel completely stuffed and uncomfortable.
How often do these nighttime eating episodes happen? Do they occur at least once a week for several months?

Yeah, I'd say for the last three months, it's been happening pretty consistently, usually after a late work event. Like last Thursday, we had that product launch party, and the caterers—oh, I mentioned the caterer earlier, didn't I? Well, they finally sent the invoice, but they charged us for an extra hour of staffing that we didn't even use! I had to get on the phone with their manager, this guy named Kevin, who sounded like he was half asleep. I mean, the sheer incompetence I have to deal with on a daily basis is staggering. 

And then I get home, and Greg is complaining about the Wi-Fi being slow because he's trying to stream some golf tournament, and I just couldn't deal with it. Speaking of the Wi-Fi, we really need to switch providers. The internet has been an absolute nightmare in our neighborhood since the city did that road work on Maple Street. They dug up half the sidewalk and left these ugly orange cones everywhere for weeks. It's a complete eyesore, and the HOA hasn't done a single thing about it, even though Susan—the one with the cardboard snacks I was telling you about—is on the board. She's completely useless when it actually matters, but if your grass is half an inch too long, she's leaving a citation in your mailbox... 

Oh, gosh, I'm sorry, I'm doing it again. You asked how often the eating happens. Right. So, yeah, for the last three months, there's been at least one night almost every week where I end up eating like this, usually after one of those arguments with Greg or a late work thing. And honestly, some weeks it happens twice.
Do these nighttime eating episodes cause you a lot of distress, or interfere with your daily life in any way?

It really does. I mean, I’m still keeping up with work, which is a miracle considering the new temp they assigned to my department. She spends half the day on TikTok. I literally caught her trying to film one of those dance trends in the breakroom right next to the espresso machine. And the espresso machine has been broken for three weeks, by the way, because someone tried to froth that super thick oat milk and completely clogged the nozzle. I’ve sent three emails to facilities about it, but they are just dragging their feet. It’s like, how am I supposed to launch a national marketing campaign without caffeine? 

But anyway, yeah... the mornings after I eat like that, I just feel completely drained. And ashamed, really. It’s gotten to the point where I’ve started skipping my personal plans because I just don’t want to face anyone. I used to go to this great Saturday morning yoga class, and I had dedicated creative time for my watercolor painting, but lately I just cancel. 

Though, honestly, the yoga instructor was getting on my nerves anyway. She started burning this really intense patchouli incense that gives me a migraine, and last week she tried to sell me a twenty-dollar piece of rose quartz before class. I mean, I told her I could get the exact same rock on Amazon for five bucks with Prime shipping. The markup is just insulting... 

Wait, sorry, I'm getting off track again. But yes, it definitely interferes. I manage to push through for my job, but in my personal life, I just hide away the next day because I feel too terrible about myself to see anyone.
During these nighttime eating episodes, do you feel like you're completely out of control, like you can't stop eating even if you want to?

Yeah, that's exactly what it feels like. Once I start, especially after a really tense night with Greg... and we've been having a lot of those lately because he refuses to hire a contractor to fix the back deck. He insists he can do it himself, but the wood has been rotting since last summer, and every time I bring it up, he just gets defensive and starts complaining about how much I spend on my watercolor supplies. Which, by the way, is completely unfair because good quality Kolinsky sable brushes are an investment, and I haven't bought a new one in months. But he’ll happily drop hundreds on new golf clubs without blinking an eye. It’s the double standard that really gets to me. I mean, we both work full time, but somehow my hobbies are a waste of money and his are essential for "networking." 

But anyway... when I'm standing there in the kitchen after one of those arguments, it’s like the decision-making part of my brain just goes completely offline. I’ll literally be thinking to myself, "Patricia, stop, this is enough," but my hand just keeps reaching for more, and I can't seem to make myself stop.
Do you often find yourself eating even when you're not physically hungry, or do you sometimes eat alone because you're embarrassed about how much you're eating?

I don't really know if I'm physically hungry or not when it happens. I don't think I even stop to check if my stomach is actually growling, you know? I'm just so wound up. And as for eating alone... well, I am alone, but I wouldn't say it's because I'm trying to hide it out of embarrassment. It's mostly just because Greg goes to bed at 9:30 on the dot. 

He has this absurd commute now because they relocated his division to the corporate park out in Westlake. I told him he should just negotiate for a hybrid schedule, especially since gas prices are absolutely ridiculous right now. I filled up my SUV yesterday and it was nearly eighty dollars! And the gas station on the corner of our street is always a total nightmare to get in and out of because they designed the pump lanes completely wrong. Whoever engineered that lot clearly never drove a car larger than a Prius. You have to do a three-point turn just to get back onto the main road, and half the time there's a delivery truck blocking the exit anyway. 

But anyway, yeah. He's fast asleep by the time I'm in the kitchen. He sleeps like a rock, too, snoring loud enough to wake the dead. I've told him a hundred times he needs to get evaluated for a CPAP machine, but he absolutely refuses to go to a doctor. So, no, I'm not really sneaking away to eat by myself because I'm embarrassed about the food, he's just already passed out. And I really couldn't tell you about the hunger thing. I just haven't noticed.
